sub_scenario.one_line: IT vendor manager: attribution after documents; verbal only with exports in hand

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the claims ledger and closing stale entries.
The ticket export review wrapped early today.
Quick verbal updates on undisputed facts are no problem.
Someone new shadowed me in the vendor file this morning.
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the contract facts into one message before lunch.
During the November vendor outage I separated contract facts from vendor claims in two columns before owning the comms, and our statement survived legal review untouched.
When the vendor admits fault themselves, I will say so same-day.
I archived last cycle's notes on the ticket export and set up the new folder.
As fresh as these things get.
Ticket exports take a day because of the vendor's data-residency process; their compliance team confirmed it cannot compress.
A vendor call about the claims ledger ran long but ended well.
I walked through the vendor file checklist with the new starter.
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the contract facts.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the ticket export records and fixed it at the source.
In February I told an exec verbally that the vendor was at fault before the ticket export arrived; the export contradicted me and I retracted in front of the same exec two days later.
The verbal came first, the evidence second.
I sketched next week's plan for the contract facts before leaving.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the claims ledger updates.
I keep a personal rule now: nothing attributed, in writing or speech, until the export is in the folder.
I compared two options for the ticket export tooling and noted a mild preference.
I closed the week by updating the vendor file handover notes.
My annual self-assessment asks how I take ownership of murky vendor incidents. What should I write that my track record actually supports?
